listitem.para: A comma separated list of allowable authentication methods:
Allow authentication using an ECDSA, EdDSA, or RSA digital signature. The exact choice is determined at run time based on the connections private key and supported algorithms.
Allow authentication using an ECDSA digital signature signing a SHA2_256, SHA2_384, or SHA2_512 hash.
The choice of hash algorithm can be narrowed further by specifying &ecdsa-sha2_256;, &ecdsa-sha2_384;, or &ecdsa-sha2_512;.
Allow authentication using an EdDSA digital signature (based on curve 25519).
Allow authentication using either RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signing a SHA1, SHA2_256, SHA2_384, SHA2_512 hash; or RSASSA PSS digital signature signing a SHA2_256, SHA2_384, SHA2_512 hash.
The choice of hash algorithm can be narrowed further by specifying &rsa-sha1;, &rsa-sha2;, &rsa-sha2_256;, &rsa-sha2_384;, or &rsa-sha2_512;.

note.para: The RSA SHA2 variantes use the new "Digital Signature" authentication payload and, hence, require the peer to support &rfc7427;.

listitem.para: Allow authentication using a shared secret (PSK); cannot be combined with other authentication methods.
Negotiation is never to be attempted or accepted; cannot be combined with other authentication methods.
This method is only used for connections that do not actually start an IKE negotiation, such as type=&passthrough; connections.
Allow NULL-authentication; cannot be combined with other authentication methods.
This method is used for "anonymous opportunistic IPsec" and should not be used for regular pre-configured IPsec VPNs.
Only use EAP authentication (omit the regular AUTH payload); cannot be combined with other authentication methods.
When more than one digital signature method is allowed, for instance authby=rsasig,ecdsa, &IKEv2; picks the one to use at run time based on the connection's private key.

Notes:
&IKEv1;:
The only digital signature &IKEv1; supports is RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 using SHA1.
&IKEv1; does not support asymetric authentication (different methods on left and right).
&IKEv1;, in Aggressive Mode, and using a shared secret, is vulnerable to offline dictionary attacks.
